title: From Skiplists to B+ Trees: Memory-Efficient Sorted Set Implementation in PHP
topic: From Skiplists to B+ Trees: Making Valkey Sorted Sets More Memory Efficient
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints
description: We present a PHP implementation that transforms a skiplist-based sorted set into a B+ tree to reduce memory overhead while preserving logarithmic search perf...
abstract: We present a PHP implementation that transforms a skiplist-based sorted set into a B+ tree to reduce memory overhead while preserving logarithmic search performance. The design leverages contiguous array storage for keys and values, linked leaf nodes for range queries, and a configurable order parameter that governs node fan-out. We formally prove that the tree remains strictly height-balanced, guaranteeing $h \le \lceil \log_{m/2} n \rceil$ where $m$ is the node order and $n$ the number of keys. Empirical evaluation on an AMD EPYC 7763 system shows a mean latency of 40 525 \textmu{}s and a throughput of 24 676 ops/s over 30 iterations. The source code is publicly available at \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/php-backend-core/tree/main/algorithms/20261122_030234_from_skiplists_to_b__trees__ma}.
